Clear an atlas's build cache

Source: R/clear_cache.R
clear_atlas_cache.Rd

Removes the intermediates a build left under output_dir, so the next run recomputes from the source files rather than reusing anything.

A build reuses what it finds, which is what makes skip_existing worth having on a pipeline that takes minutes. The cache knows the format that wrote it, the version of this package, and what each step was given, and recomputes when any of those move. It cannot know that a source file was regenerated in place within the same second and at the same size, or that you want to see a build from nothing. Clear it when you want to be sure.

Usage

clear_atlas_cache(
  atlas_name = NULL,
  output_dir = get_output_dir(),
  force = FALSE
)

Arguments

atlas_name

Name of the atlas whose cache to clear. NULL clears every atlas under output_dir, which is only sensible when output_dir is a directory kept for builds.

output_dir

Where the build wrote its intermediates. Defaults to the ggseg.extra.output_dir option, as a build does.

force

Remove the directory even when it holds files this package did not write. FALSE, the default, refuses rather than delete your data.

Value

Invisibly, the paths removed.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# after changing a lookup table the pipeline cannot see into
clear_atlas_cache("shen268_subcortical", output_dir = "data-raw")

# start a build from nothing
clear_atlas_cache("glasser", output_dir = "data-raw")
create_cortical_from_annotation(annot, atlas_name = "glasser")
} # }
